clue.text: Advisor who's not welcome to dine in rugby players' club

indicators.note: the dining word is placed in the middle of the rugby players' club, between its two halves

parts.note: the backs are the rugby players behind the scrum
a driver is a golf club

explanation.surface: Someone eating at a rugby club offers advice nobody asked for.
explanation.definitionFit: A back-seat driver gives unwanted directions from the rear of a car, hence any unwelcome adviser.

clue.text: Gutless emperor trembled after very macho glance

indicators.note: the emperor and trembling pieces come after the macho piece in the answer
removing the guts of a word leaves only its outside letters

explanation.surface: A cowardly ruler shivered after a tough-guy stare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gutless' strips EMPEROR to its outer letters ER. A butcher's hook is Cockney rhyming slang: butcher's hook rhymes with look.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang a butcher's (hook) is a look, so a quick glance.

clue.text: Stick characters in erotic lingerie

indicators.note: the letters sit among the characters of the following two words

explanation.surface: Racy underwear that clings to the body.
explanation.definitionFit: To cling is to stick fast to something, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Takes off part of the weekend, given flowers

parts.note: Sat is short for Saturday, part of the weekend

explanation.surface: Someone takes a weekend day off and is given a bouquet.
explanation.definitionFit: To take off someone is to mimic and mock them, which is what a satirist does.

clue.text: What pretentious people put on, hot in transport

parts.note: hot in the sense fashionable is hip

explanation.surface: Pretentious people putting on airs while travelling.
explanation.definitionFit: An airship is a lighter-than-air craft, a means of transport.

clue.text: Ate up most of ham, in reality

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from the bottom
the last letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a ham is a bad actor

explanation.surface: Someone really did eat most of the ham.
explanation.definitionFit: De facto is Latin for existing in fact, as opposed to by right or law.

clue.text: Bull's neighbour has meal first off

indicators.note: the opening letter of the meal word comes off

explanation.surface: A neighbour of a bull eats first.
explanation.walkthrough: The bull is the bullseye on a dartboard, not an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: On a dartboard the inner ring surrounds the bullseye, its immediate neighbour.

clue.text: A must see: Stalin getting overthrown

indicators.note: an overthrown arrangement is upset, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Seeing Stalin toppled is essential viewing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is a must is indispensable, which is what essential means as a noun.

clue.text: Corrupt leaders in thrash arranged inside Number Ten

indicators.note: the leaders are the opening letters of the next three words

parts.note: T is short for ten, as in T for a ten-pound note or ten in some notations

explanation.surface: A beating arranged inside Downing Street corrupts the government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' looks like an insertion signal but is just a third word whose first letter is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: To taint is to contaminate or corrupt something, a synonym as a verb.

clue.text: Official to an extent securing home cover again

indicators.note: the official and extent pieces hold the home word between them

parts.note: a ref is a referee, an official

explanation.surface: A referee partly secures a home's covering again.
explanation.definitionFit: To refinish is to give a surface a new coat or finish, covering it again.

clue.text: Old browser? A bot runs ours loosely

indicators.note: the letters are arranged loosely, that is rearranged freely

explanation.surface: An old web browser? A bot runs ours.
explanation.walkthrough: A browser here is an animal that browses plants, not internet software.
explanation.definitionFit: The brontosaurus was a long-necked plant-eating dinosaur, an extinct browser of leaves.

clue.text: Artist drawing horse behind farm animal

indicators.note: the drawing and horse pieces come behind the farm animal

parts.note: H is slang for heroin, which is also called horse

explanation.surface: An artist sketches a horse behind a pig.
explanation.walkthrough: William Hogarth was an 18th-century English painter and satirical engraver.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogarth is an example of an artist, famous for The Rake's Progress.

clue.text: He investigates passing round pickle sandwiches

indicators.note: the pickle word holds the round letter inside like a filling

parts.note: in a pickle means in a corner, a difficult situation

explanation.surface: A detective looks at round sandwiches being handed over with pickle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passing' belongs to the definition: a passing is a death.
explanation.definitionFit: A coroner holds inquests into deaths whose cause is unclear.

clue.text: What must be cracked on vehicle

explanation.surface: Something must be broken on a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebus is a picture puzzle, something to be solved or cracked.

clue.text: British recalling space traveller's instrument

parts.note: a la means in the style of, so recalling something
Laika was the Soviet dog sent into orbit in 1957; the 's links to the definition

explanation.surface: A Brit remembers an astronaut's musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A balalaika is a Russian stringed instrument with a triangular body.

clue.text: Expert insight for furnishing

explanation.surface: A professional offers insight into furnishing a home.
explanation.definitionFit: Provision is the act of supplying or furnishing something.

clue.text: Getting cross, perhaps, in my play area before time

parts.note: cor is an exclamation like my!
a rec is a recreation ground

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper at the playground before it's time.
explanation.walkthrough: A wrong answer gets a cross from the marker; 'perhaps' signals that example.
explanation.definitionFit: An incorrect answer is marked with a cross, so getting a cross means being wrong.

clue.text: Husband has problems stifling camp inclinations

indicators.note: the problems word smothers the camp word inside it

parts.note: a camp is a side or faction

explanation.surface: A husband's troubles keep his camp tendencies suppressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Hillsides are slopes, and an inclination can mean a slope or incline.

clue.text: Land's ground seemed to contain nitrogen

definitions.note: the definition is Land with 's for is joining it to the wordplay

indicators.note: the shuffled letters hold the nitrogen letter within them
ground in the sense of crushed, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: Soil on an estate appeared to contain nitrogen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' rearranges SEEMED to DEMESE, around N.
explanation.definitionFit: A demesne is land attached to a manor and kept by its owner, an estate.

clue.text: Bulb, one often lit up around foyer

indicators.note: the drunk word goes around the foyer word

parts.note: lit up means drunk, and a sot is a drunkard

explanation.surface: A light bulb glows around a lobby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lit up' suggests a light bulb, but it means drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallot is a small onion-like vegetable that grows as a bulb.

clue.text: Business chief pockets £50 in big fiddle?

indicators.note: the chief executive puts the money letters in his pocket, inside his letters

parts.note: L stands for pound (£) and L is the Roman numeral 50

explanation.surface: A company boss pockets fifty pounds in a large fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddle' looks like a fraud but is a violin.
explanation.definitionFit: A cello is a large member of the violin family, and a violin is informally a fiddle.

clue.text: It stores crude ancient booze tucked into by setter

indicators.note: the setter letter is tucked inside the ancient booze

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: Something holds rough old liquor that the setter is drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: Crude here is crude oil, not rough.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil drum is a large barrel used to store crude oil.

clue.text: Plant once again lush, climbing

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means the word reads from the bottom

parts.note: a lush is a drunkard, a toper

explanation.surface: A lush plant climbs again.
explanation.definitionFit: To repot a plant is to plant it once again in a new pot.

clue.text: Sign of virtue from samurai, periodically welcoming new role

indicators.note: the alternate letters take the reworked role inside
taking letters at regular intervals from the warrior word
new means remade, so these letters are reformed

explanation.surface: A samurai shows virtue by accepting a new role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'periodically' takes AUA from samurai; 'new' makes REOL of role.
explanation.definitionFit: An aureola is a halo of light round a saint's head, a symbol of holiness.

clue.text: Boutros Boutros-Ghali's repeated conclusion

indicators.note: the letters are hidden within the name, and appear repeated since Boutros occurs twice

explanation.surface: The UN Secretary-General's name, with its repetition, as a finish.
explanation.walkthrough: Boutros Boutros-Ghali was UN Secretary-General 1992-96; the run of letters is in each Boutros.
explanation.definitionFit: An outro is the closing section of a song or broadcast, its conclusion.

clue.text: Chucking away soggy food, about to stuff face

indicators.note: the reversed food is stuffed into the face word
about means turned round, so read backwards

parts.note: sops are pieces of soaked bread

explanation.surface: Someone throws away soggy food before cramming their face.
explanation.definitionFit: Disposal is the act of getting rid of something, of throwing it away.

clue.text: Tea drunk by queen in Royal Gala, say

indicators.note: the jumbled tea goes in the queen's letters
drunk means reeling, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: The queen drinks tea at a royal gala.
explanation.walkthrough: Royal Gala is a variety of apple, not a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A Royal Gala is a dessert apple, an eater as opposed to a cooker.

clue.text: Positions men take up in Waterloo and Austerlitz?

definitions.meaning: where troops go when ready for combat
both are battles and both are railway stations, in London and Paris

explanation.surface: Where soldiers deployed in two Napoleonic battles.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterloo and Austerlitz are Napoleonic battles as well as London and Paris railway stations, so battle stations.
